description: Quantum gate library reference for the 3-qubit QFT circuit (8-bit datapath). Verified CIRCT/Chisel-generated wrapper modules for QSV state-vector simulation hardware. Use this as the authoritative list of available gates, their module names, ports, and behavior. Circuits instantiate these 3QubitVector8bit WRAPPER modules (never primitive gates directly).

encoding.format: QSV — Quantum State Vector (3 qubits, 8 basis states)
encoding.amplitude: 8 amplitudes QSV_0..QSV_7 for |000>..|111>. Each amplitude is a complex pair of 8-bit signals: suffix _0 = real, _1 = imaginary.
encoding.fixed_point: 8-bit signed fixed point (this circuit uses an 8-bit datapath). NOTE: confirm exact Q-format (e.g. Q1.7) with library owner.
encoding.valid_protocol: Every gate has io_in_valid / io_out_valid. Chain stages by connecting each stage's io_in_valid to the previous stage's io_out_valid. Gates handle valid internally — add no extra logic.

gates.name: HGate3QubitVector8bit
gates.applies_to: one target qubit of the 3-qubit register
gates.behavior: Hadamard: creates superposition on the target qubit. |0>->(|0>+|1>)/sqrt2, |1>->(|0>-|1>)/sqrt2. Adder/subtractor + 1/sqrt2 constant multiplier. Applied across the 8-amplitude state vector.
gates.latency_note: CONFIRM: parent paper Table 1 says H=3; observed wrapper latency in prior sims was 5.

gates.name: CSGate3QubitVector8bit
gates.behavior: Controlled-S: applies an S phase (pi/2) to the target amplitude only when the control qubit is |1>. Phase rotation; multiply by i on the |11> component of the controlled pair.
gates.port_pruning_note: VERIFIED against QFTcircuit_8bit_NC.sv (2026-07-18): io_in_QSV_3_1 and io_in_QSV_7_1 are NOT present on the real compiled module. CIRCT proved the imaginary component feeding this CS instance is always zero at this point in the circuit and eliminated those two input ports entirely -- they are pruned/tied-off in this compilation, not an omission. The port list below reflects the real module exactly. Note for future circuits: a model producing the full-port (unpruned) version would be functionally correct hardware but will fail exact-match compile against this specific optimized baseline -- a real limitation of exact-match verification, not a defect in that hypothetical output.

gates.name: CTGate3QubitVector8bit
gates.behavior: Controlled-T: applies a T phase (pi/4, e^(i*pi/4)=(1+i)/sqrt2) to the target amplitude only when the control qubit is |1>. Requires a multiplier.
gates.latency_note: CONFIRM latency with library owner (contains a multiplier; may be multi-cycle).

gates.name: SWGate3QubitVector8bit
gates.behavior: SWAP: exchanges the states of two qubits (used in QFT to reverse qubit order). Pure wiring — reorders amplitudes, no arithmetic.

gates.name: CompatiblePerm
gates.behavior: Permutation layer. Reorders the state-vector amplitudes so a gate's target qubit is mapped to the default position (q0 for single-qubit, (q1,q0) for two-qubit). Insert before AND after any gate whose target is not already in the default position, then a matching perm to restore ordering. Pure wiring.
gates.variants_note: This circuit contains multiple perm variants: CompatiblePerm, CompatiblePerm_1, CompatiblePerm_2 (they reorder different qubit positions at size 8 — e.g. swap positions 3&2, 3&1, 2&1). Use the variant that maps the specific target qubit to the default position.

usage_notes.wrapper_rule: Instantiate ONLY the *3QubitVector8bit wrapper modules and CompatiblePerm — never the primitive gates (HadamardGate, ControlledSGate, ControlledTGate, SwapGate) directly.
usage_notes.perm_rule: Insert a CompatiblePerm before and after any gate whose target qubit is not in the default position. Gates on q0 (and the default two-qubit position) need no perm.
unconfirmed: which CompatiblePerm variant maps which qubit position
